name: Quality HVAC by Fibid
verdict: Over the past 28 days, Quality HVAC by Fibid generated 8 leads at a $223.26 CPL across $1,786.10 in total spend, with Google Ads leading investment at $1,113.97. The biggest movement is a 100% drop in GBP engagement week-over-week, likely reflecting a pause or data gap in the Google Business Profile, while overall spend also pulled back 21.77% in the last 7 days, driven largely by a 39.23% reduction in Google Ads spend.

performance.verdict: Six overdue milestones now block scaling; spend throttle is masking real CPL risk.

findings.text: Booking bot battle-test (due 2026-07-31), intake owner confirmation, Review Boost campaign, Financing page, Homer Glen branch (all due 2026-08-31), and LSA heating re-enable (due 2026-09-01) are all overdue — 6 milestones outstanding.
28-day CPL is $223.26 across only 8 leads; 3-day lead signal (Sep 6–8: 0+1+1=2 leads) vs prior 3 days (Sep 3–5: 2+1+0=3 leads) shows no improvement and volume is threadbare against $59.86/day spend.
GBP actions hit zero for 8 consecutive days (Sep 1–8, from 98 actions in the prior 28-day window) — a -100% WoW drop suggesting the profile is suppressed or data-dark, not a paid issue.

Google Ads spend dropped -39.23% WoW; 3-day Google spend (Sep 6–8: $24.14+$107.82+$12.33=$144.29) vs prior 3 (Sep 3–5: $22.79+$23.16+$24.14=$70.09) is volatile, spiking on Sep 7 then collapsing — campaign pacing is erratic, not a deliberate throttle shape.
GHL shows 80 opportunities created but 0 appointments recorded against 264 contacts — speed-to-lead automation may be routing to the vacated Vivian dispatch seat, losing booked jobs.

suggestions.text: Confirm and reassign GHL intake seat vacated by Vivian; audit speed-to-lead routing — 0 appointments vs 80 opportunities is a confirmed intake leak.
suggestions.monday_update: Vivian (dispatch) left 7/7 and the intake owner milestone is overdue since 8/31. GHL shows 80 opportunities created and 0 appointments booked against 264 contacts — every lead routed to an empty seat is a lost job. Nacer to confirm the new intake owner, update their GHL login, verify after-hours coverage, and re-point all speed-to-lead automations to the active seat. Success check: at least 1 appointment recorded in GHL within 7 days of the fix, confirmed by 2026-09-16.

suggestions.text: Investigate GBP profile — 8 straight days of zero actions (Sep 1–8) vs 98 actions in prior 28 days; rule out suspension or NAP mismatch before LSA re-enable.
suggestions.monday_update: GBP actions have been zero every day from Sep 1–8 (8 consecutive days), down from 98 actions over the prior 28-day window — a -100% WoW drop. Check the Crestwood and primary profiles for any suspension notice, NAP inconsistency, or ownership issue (do not touch the Crestwood 145-review profile). This must be resolved before LSA heating toggle is re-enabled, as a suppressed GBP will undercut LSA ranking. Confirm profile status and document findings by 2026-09-12.

suggestions.text: Watch Meta CPL trend through Sep 12; Meta is sole confirmed lead source (8/8 leads) but 3-day volume (2 leads) is too thin to scale without intact intake routing.
suggestions.monday_update: Meta has generated all 8 confirmed leads over the 28-day window at a $223.26 CPL, but the last 3 days (Sep 6–8) produced only 2 leads — volume is thin and intake routing is broken per F5. Do not scale Meta budget until the GHL intake seat is confirmed active (S1) and the CPL baseline can be measured against a functioning funnel. Re-check on 2026-09-12: if intake is fixed and CPL holds below $250 over the next 3 days, bring a scale recommendation.
